title: Concrete SPN t-Wise Independence
summary: Existing concrete-S-box SPN results address only pairwise independence; the open task is to characterize fixed layers that yield higher t-wise independence.

formal_statement.body: For substitution-permutation networks (SPNs) with $t$-wise independence as the security goal, prior constructions of $t$-wise-independent permutations are far from existing practical designs, and existing results for SPNs instantiated with concrete S-boxes address only pairwise independence. Identify concrete, fixed choices of the nonlinear and linear layers and prove which choices yield $t$-wise independence and which do not, without modeling the S-box as a random permutation oracle; in particular, establish $t$-wise independence for such networks for every $t \ge 3$. Under the independent-round-keys assumption for SPNs, $t$-wise independence is expected to become $t$-wise pseudorandomness when the key schedule is instantiated appropriately; determine the precise role of the key schedule by characterizing which concrete instantiations support this transition and under what conditions. Prove that multi-round AES with independent round keys is $t$-wise independent for $t>2$. For the AES design, existing bounds make differential probabilities arbitrarily close to the ideal value $2^{-128}$ by first controlling statistical distance; derive a direct bound on these differential probabilities that does not proceed through a statistical-distance bound.

scope.domain: The design and analysis of symmetric block ciphers, focusing on concrete SPN nonlinear and linear layers and t-wise independence.
assumptions: Independent round keys for SPNs, including the multi-round AES case.
The S-box is not modeled as a random permutation oracle.
parameters: The nonlinear and linear layer choices, the concrete SPN components to classify
The key schedule, whose concrete instantiation determines support for the transition to t-wise pseudorandomness
AES's 128-bit block size, which sets the ideal differential-probability value
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine which concrete fixed nonlinear and linear layers yield or fail to yield t-wise independence for every t >= 3; characterize key-schedule instantiations supporting the transition to t-wise pseudorandomness; prove the multi-round AES claim for t > 2; and derive a direct AES differential-probability bound without an intermediate statistical-distance bound.

progress.summary: The source presents this as part of its research program, asking which concrete fixed nonlinear and linear SPN layers work and requiring analysis without modeling the S-box as a random permutation oracle. It contrasts this broader program with concrete results addressing pairwise independence.
citation_labels: Tianren Liu et al., The $t$-wise Independence of Substitution-Permutation Networks
